reader_question: How far apart are homeownership rates by race, and has the gap closed?
title: Non-Hispanic White and Black homeownership rates were nearly 30 points apart in 2025, a wider gap than in 2003.
reading_guide: Each panel draws one group as a heavy line over the other three as thin gray lines, on one scale, so the gaps read across panels.
measure_line: Households that own their home, percent, by race and ethnicity of householder, annual averages, United States, 1994 to 2025. Every panel runs from 40 to 80 percent.
notes: The gap between non-Hispanic White and Black households widened from 27.3 points in 2003 to 29.6 in 2025, by 2.3 points, more than the change’s margin of error of about 0.7. The gap to Hispanic households narrowed from 28.7 points to 25.8, also by more than its margin.

The lines break where the Census changed its method: in 2002 it reweighted its estimates to the 2000 Census, so that year shows two values, and in 2003 it changed its race categories, so the Black and non-Hispanic White lines start again.
The Census Bureau asks readers to use caution comparing 2020 with other years, after interviews moved to the phone.
Margins of error, at 90 percent, run from 0.2 to 0.5 points for each group’s rate in 2003 and 2025, from the Bureau’s Table B-7; Oath & Action computed the gaps’ margins from them.
source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Current Population Survey/Housing Vacancy Survey, Annual Statistics 2025, Table 22, homeownership rate by race and ethnicity of householder, 1994 to 2025, with margins from Table B-7 of the 2003 and 2025 Annual Statistics, United States. Retrieved November 6 and 11, 2026. Race categories changed in 2003; pandemic changes to data collection affect 2020; the 2025 average leaves out October, when no data were collected; margins of the gaps computed by Oath & Action.
alt: Four small line charts of the homeownership rate from 1994 to 2025, one each for all households, non-Hispanic White, Hispanic and Black householders, on one scale from 40 to 80 percent. In 2025 the rates were 65.2, 74.3, 48.5 and 44.7 percent; the gap between non-Hispanic White and Black households grew from 27.3 points in 2003 to 29.6 in 2025.

table.caption: Homeownership rate by race and ethnicity of householder, percent

chart_notes: Gray lines: the other three groups. Each panel heads with the group and its 2025 rate.
Gaps to non-Hispanic White households: Hispanic, 28.7 points in 2003 and 25.8 in 2025; Black, 27.3 points in 2003 and 29.6 in 2025.
